fun_facts: Saquon Barkley’s birthplace is Coplay, Pennsylvania.
In high school, Saquon Barkley played football, basketball, and track.
In 2015, Saquon Barkley won the 100-meter race at the Eastern Pennsylvania Conference track and field championships.
Saquon Barkley gave away the first gold medal he won as a high school sprinter.
At Penn State, Saquon Barkley set school records with 5,538 all-purpose yards, 53 total touchdowns, and 43 rushing touchdowns; he was also a two-time Big Ten Offensive Player of the Year.
As a kid, Saquon Barkley admired Barry Sanders, kept a Sanders action figure in his bedroom, and practiced running side to side like him.

basis.reasoning: The ESPN biography identifies Saquon Barkley’s college as Penn State.

excerpts: Barkley was a three-sport athlete in football, basketball and track at Whitehall High School in Whitehall Township, Pennsylvania. Barkley, four-star recruit, was ranked as high as the No. 6 overall running back in the country and the No. 1 player in Pennsylvania, depending on the recruiting service, in the class of 2015.

excerpts:
It's not on the football field.

It was May 2015, and Barkley won the 100 meters in the Eastern Pennsylvania Conference track and field championships.
Barkley smiles. This is the guy who gave away the first gold medal he won as a high school sprinter. Who deadlifts more than defensive linemen, who runs faster than ... almost anyone.
citations.title: Penn State's Saquon Barkley putting distance between himself and peers

excerpts: Barkley rushed for 3,843 yards and was the two-time Big Ten Offensive Player of the Year at Penn State. His 5,538 all-purpose yards, 53 total touchdowns and 43 rushing touchdowns were school records. The Giants were enamored with Barkley from the start of the process, and their offseason moves sent them in the direction of the draft's top running back.
citations.title: Saquon Barkley taken by Giants at No. 2 as team bolsters offensive attack - ESPN

excerpts:
_Where is he?_

It's the third quarter of the 2017 Rose Bowl, and Penn State's running back has just juked a USC defender near the line of scrimmage at his own 20. As a kid, Barkley had loved Barry Sanders, even keeping a Sanders action figure in his bedroom. Growing up, he'd run to one side, then the other, trying to perfect Sanders' Houdini act, an early experiment in lateral quickness that ultimately led him here, in Pasadena, on the verge of breaking a big run.
